## Oral Mechanism Examination & Clinical Swallow Assessment

Today's simulation focuses on cranial nerve function, oral mechanism examination (OME), and clinical decision-making in dysphagia assessment.

Students will apply evidence from assigned readings, practice examination skills with peers, and explore the role of instrumental swallowing assessments in acute care.
:::

::: {.warning}
## SLP Task

Work collaboratively to review cranial nerve function, complete simulated oral mechanism examinations, and interpret clinical findings.

Throughout the session, consider what information can be obtained through bedside assessment, what limitations remain, and when additional assessment may be warranted.
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, students will be able to:

- Identify cranial nerves relevant to speech, swallowing, and airway protection.
- Demonstrate components of a focused oral mechanism examination.
- Interpret oral mechanism findings in relation to swallowing function.
- Discuss the clinical utility and limitations of the OME in predicting aspiration.
- Adapt examination procedures based on patient presentation and communication abilities.
- Compare the purposes, strengths, and limitations of clinical swallow evaluation, FEES, and MBSS.
- Apply clinical reasoning to determine when instrumental assessment may be indicated.
- Integrate evidence from assigned readings into clinical decision-making.

---

## Today's Modules

### 1. Cranial Nerves & Oral Mechanism Examination

Review cranial nerves relevant to speech and swallowing, their associated functions, and methods of assessment.

Test your knowledge and practice components of a focused oral mechanism examination with a partner.

[Begin Cranial Nerve Review](cranial-nerves.html)

### 2. Oral Mechanism Case Practice

Work with a partner to complete simulated oral mechanism examinations using four acute care patient scenarios.

Alternate roles as the SLP and patient while practicing examination techniques, interpreting findings, and discussing clinical implications.

[Begin Case Practice](case-studies.html)

### 3. Bedside Assessment & Instrumentation

Compare clinical swallow evaluation, FEES, and MBSS.

Apply evidence from assigned readings and clinical scenarios to determine which assessment approach best addresses the clinical question.

[Compare Assessment Options](instrumentation.html)
